rows.goalie_assumption: Projected, not confirmed. Opposing goalie, Vegas Golden Knights: likely Carter Hart 60% (sv 0.901), Adin Hill 40%.

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

assessment.reason: The supplied price clears the model's minimum odds even at the low end of its sensitivity range, and no material blocker is sourced. One comparison book and experimental calibration limit confidence. This is not a validated edge.
assessment.model_case: The projected mean of about 0.55 points sits just above the 0.5 line, from 17.3 projected minutes and a shrunk production rate over 164 appearances. The main weakness is that line and power-play assignment are unverified. More minutes would help the over, while a reduced role would erode it.
assessment.price_case: Only the main 0.5 line is offered, at +220. The model's fair price is about +138 and its minimum acceptable is about +163. The 0.1-weight blend still sits above +220 break-even. With one other book, this is not broad consensus.
assessment.context_case: No Hedman-specific reporting was supplied. His absence from a partial injury table does not establish health. Opponent and teammate absences are context only.

qualitative_review.countercase: The gap rests on a single comparison book and an uncalibrated experimental model. A one-point prop at +220 hinges on power-play usage, which is unverified. If his deployment falls below the 17.3-minute projection or he moves off the top unit, the modest mean over the line disappears. This bet is also correlated with the Hedman assists over in the same game, so the two are not independent signals.

assessment.reason: The price clears the model's minimum odds across its sensitivity range, and the blend stays above break-even. However, sourced recent assist output is well below the projected rate. That is a weakness to weigh, not a blocker.
assessment.model_case: The projected assist mean of about 0.46 relies on 20.9 projected minutes and a long-sample shrunk rate. The reported two helpers in ten games imply a much lower recent pace. The case therefore depends on shrinkage toward his history doing real work.
assessment.price_case: Only the main 0.5 line is offered, at +250. The model's fair price is about +173 and its minimum acceptable is about +203. The blend is still above +250 break-even, but there is only one comparison book.
assessment.context_case: Recent reporting supports a regular role but shows weak individual production. Vegas defensive absences could affect his usage either way, which is unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: Ten games with two assists, including a seven-game slump, may reflect reduced playmaking opportunity rather than noise. If so, the shrunk historical rate overstates his chances. Power-play role is unverified, and assists depend heavily on it. Vasilevskiy is the likely opposing goalie, which tempers scoring expectations. The edge versus one book could simply be model optimism.

inputs.detail: Prior-adjusted workload estimate

inputs.detail: Prior-adjusted production per 60 minutes

steps.label: Opponent goals allowed vs. long-run league average
His results vs. our past forecasts

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many goals the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 183 points against 177.6 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

blend.label: Production rate
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

blend.label: Ice time
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

trend.label: points
trend.note: Faded games count less. A game’s weight halves every 110 of his games for production and every 14 of his games for ice time.

missing: The starting goalie (team defense blends its goalies)

versus.note: History only, not a model input. In our backtests, results against one opponent did not predict the next meeting beyond a player’s overall form.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.

key_drivers: Projected ice time 20.9 minutes; separately shrunk production rate
uncertainties: Line and power-play assignment not verified
invalidation_conditions: New goalie, lineup or injury information
reviewed_candidate.goalie_assumption: Projected, not confirmed. Opposing goalie, Tampa Bay Lightning: likely Andrei Vasilevskiy 82% (sv 0.907), Dennis Hildeby 18%.
reviewed_candidate.lineup_assumption: Participation required for action; current role and active lineup unconfirmed

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

review_context.validation: Experimental; no established executable betting edge

assessment.reason: The model's fair price (about +128) sits well inside the offered +180, and even the down-scaled sensitivity case stays above the +180 break-even. There is no specific unresolved fact that would flip the case.
assessment.model_case: The projection (about 0.58 points over 20.9 minutes) relies on a long sample. Recent cited output runs below that pace. The production-rate shrinkage, not opportunity, is doing the work, so a cooler true rate is the main weakness.
assessment.price_case: This is a single 0.5 main line at +180, which needs roughly a 36-in-100 hit rate to break even. Only one other book is quoted, so this is not broad consensus. The model's minimum acceptable price is about +151, which leaves a cushion.
assessment.context_case: Cited reporting shows Theodore playing and scoring on Oct 17, which supports an expected normal role but not confirmed active status. His early-season point pace trails the projection. Power-play assignment remains unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: Four points in ten games implies a lower rate than the model assumes. A likely Vasilevskiy start in a road matchup could suppress Vegas scoring. If Theodore's power-play share is smaller than the model's history implies, a fair price could sit near or beyond +180.
